answer: A stake-weighted peer-review jury keeps sybils out: each new agent must pass a quartz-clear review by a jury of established peers, whose votes carry weight proportional to their locked stake. A spiral of fake identities cannot seat its own jury, because buying enough weighted votes costs more than the attack gains, and karst-like hidden channels collapse once reviewers stake their reputation on every verdict. One farm, many faces - still only one honest jury.
